title.narrative: Climate Justice and gender -responsive livelihoods for resilient food systems

description.narrative: The Climate Justice and Gender-Responsive Livelihoods for Resilient Food Systems Project is a three-year programme (2025-2028) to be implemented by the Zambia Climate Change Network (ZCCN) in Mongu (Mawawa), Nyimba (Baloni, Mombe Ward, Ngulube Village, Vizimumba Ward, Kamono Camp), and Petauke (Kasusu Camp). The project will work with 2,000 beneficiaries, of which 70% are women and the rest are youth and men. The project aims to strengthen climate-resilient and gender-responsive food systems by supporting women, youth, and communities to build sustainable livelihoods and adapt to climate change. It will help communities develop climate-smart income activities through study circles, savings groups, and cooperatives, while improving access to finance, markets, and productive resources. Further, the project will promote agroecology, including the use of solar-powered irrigation systems for sustainable food production, fruit tree planting for nutrition and livelihood, and value chain development to improve food security and resilience. Women's leadership will be improved by addressing structural barriers in value chains, supporting land rights, and increasing participation in decision-making spaces. The project will also build community capacity for climate adaptation, environmental management, and advocacy, while strengthening ZCCN's organisational governance and accountability.
